name_note: The _A suffix marks a GTDB split within Lawsonella clevelandensis; published work uses the unsuffixed species name.

sentences.text: Lawsonella clevelandensis is a strictly anaerobic, partially acid-fast Gram-positive bacillus that was formally described in 2016.
It is increasingly reported as a cause of deep-seated abscesses, and its fastidious growth and absence from routine diagnostic databases lead to underdiagnosis.
A narrative review of documented cases notes risk factors such as diabetes, immunosuppression and prior surgery, and a predilection for fat-rich tissues.
